correctness.rationale: Writing h=−min(x,y)+(x²+y²)/2 gives Δ=∫[2x(1−F)−(1−F)²]dx. My separate symbolic replay from that identity gives d/15−c²/30−d²/210 and verifies the rational zero parametrization. The derivative lower bound 2c(1−3r)>0, positive left endpoint, and factorization F−x=−x(1−x)[c+d(2x−1)] prove admissibility and strict stochastic separation. The derivative of the doubled projection, after dropping an irrelevant constant, is 2(x−(1−F(x))); integrating and taking exact variance gives the stated V, null value 1/45 and r=1/4 fraction. The sign of the displayed derivative follows from 24255−160622/9>0; variance is positive by the nonconstant projection and the positive density. The computed 5% limit is 0.0476118698. For the different linear-density family, the exact mean is −c²/30. The bounded degenerate kernel has remainder variance O(n⁻²) uniformly: distinct unordered pairs have zero covariance even when sharing one index, by conditional centering. First-projection row variances converge to the positive null limit by uniform density/projection convergence, and boundedness gives Lindeberg. The null-scaled drift is −h² n^(1/2−2γ)/(2√5); continuity at the cutoff gives the two finite-shift cases, and tightness plus divergent negative drift gives power one otherwise. For critical nonzero shift the two-sided normal tail is strictly increasing in the absolute shift and below one. The comparison is neither a minimax bound nor a claim about censoring. value.rationale: The point is not another arbitrary nonuniform zero. A quadratic perturbation (the lowest polynomial degree permitting this cancellation among nonuniform densities) produces strictly increasing densities whose CDFs separate from uniformity in a single direction and whose rejection rate stays below the nominal level throughout the stated branch. This gives a simple calibrated, shape-restricted benchmark for a procedure intended to detect nonuniform laws. The local-power calculation gives scope and a quantitative comparison, not novelty or value by itself over the prior exact tilt drift.
